ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Calamity Jane

code.originalText: Four-week review: naltrexone and the change to a monthly injection, liver stiffness, mood after four weeks without alcohol, and benefits

text.paragraph: Four-week review: naltrexone, liver stiffness, mood and benefits. [S]

Ms. Canary returns four weeks after intake. She has had no alcohol. Her tooth was removed at the dental clinic the day after her sick visit, and she finished the amoxicillin; the pain and swelling are gone. She has missed about eight of the last 21 naltrexone tablets: a bottle was lost when she moved her things, and some days she forgot. Cravings are milder on the days she takes it. She has had no nausea or stomach pain. She sleeps five to six hours and her mood is better. Her Medicaid and SNAP have been approved. She has called the peer recovery specialist twice and went to one women's meeting. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-30; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 122/78, pulse 78; weight 50.9 kg, BMI 18.7
No jaundice, spider angiomas or palmar erythema

Alcohol use disorder, severe (nine of eleven DSM-5-TR criteria), daily drinking of about a pint of whiskey with heavier binges for many years; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented lifelong heavy drinking
S — Synthetic modern coding; DSM-5-TR severe alcohol use disorder maps to F10.20 when withdrawal is coded separately. Person-first language; not a claim about her real diagnosis.
Alcohol withdrawal, mild, at low risk of complications (PAWSS 3, CIWA-Ar 9 at intake; no past seizures or delirium tremens), managed as an outpatient with daily nurse checks
S — Synthetic withdrawal episode; resolved by the one-week visit.
Raised liver enzymes (AST 96, ALT 44, GGT 240 U/L) with a FIB-4 index of 3.93, above the cut point for possible advanced fibrosis; liver stiffness measurement planned
S — Synthetic presenting finding; superseded when elastography and the clinical picture supported alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease.
Alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease, without cirrhosis: liver stiffness 9.6 kPa after four weeks without alcohol, falling enzymes, normal bilirubin, albumin, INR and platelets
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the four-week visit.
Depressive symptoms during heavy drinking (PHQ-9 14, item 9 scored 0); whether they are alcohol-induced or an independent depression to be judged after two to four weeks without alcohol
S — Synthetic provisional finding; resolved as the PHQ-9 fell to 5 after ten weeks without alcohol, consistent with alcohol-induced depressive symptoms. Not a claim about her real mood.
Daily chewing tobacco for many years; not ready to stop at intake
S — Synthetic modern coding anchored to the documented chewing tobacco.
Underweight (BMI 18.4) with poor food intake, low folate, magnesium and phosphate, and slightly low albumin
S — Synthetic finding anchored to a contemporary impression of poor nutrition (R).
Housing instability: staying in a spare room at a friend's house, with nowhere to go if that ends; has stayed in shelters in past winters
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty and moves from town to town.
Food insecurity: often goes without meals at the end of the month
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented poverty.
Periapical abscess of a lower left molar with facial swelling and low-grade fever, on naltrexone; treated without opioids, tooth removed at the dental clinic the next day; resolved
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Severe alcohol use disorder in early recovery (F10.20). Four weeks without alcohol; PEth 24 ng/mL, down from 820, agrees with what she reports. Daily tablets are hard to keep while she moves between places, so she chose the monthly extended-release injection. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; the rifle remains with her friend. [S]
Extended-release naltrexone 380 mg intramuscularly today and every four weeks; oral naltrexone stopped.
Continue peer contact and the women's meeting.

Alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease (K70.0). Liver stiffness 9.6 kPa by transient elastography: above the 8 kPa below which advanced fibrosis is unlikely, but recent alcohol-related inflammation can raise the reading. AST 48, ALT 33 and GGT 132 U/L are falling; albumin 3.6 g/dL and platelets 191 are normal, and there are no signs of cirrhosis. FIB-4 is now 1.92. [S]
Repeat elastography and liver tests after about three more months without alcohol.
Hepatitis A and B vaccines at the preventive visit.
Acetaminophen no more than 2 g a day.

Depressive symptoms during heavy drinking (F32.A). PHQ-9 9 from 14 and GAD-7 7 from 11 after four weeks without alcohol: improving, which favors alcohol-induced symptoms. No antidepressant for now. [S]
PHQ-9 at each visit; weekly peer support; counseling offered through her new Medicaid coverage.
